XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 1. What steps is the Welsh Government taking to tackle rural poverty in Brycheiniog Tawe Nedd? OQ64579

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Member_job_title_Welsh: Y Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch am y cwestiwn.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you for the question.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: We are supporting households across Brycheiniog Tawe Nedd through targeted measures, including cost-of-living support, access to the Warm Homes programme, free school meals expansion, childcare, and funding for local authority and community-based schemes that provide access to advice, services and financial support.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Rural poverty in mid Wales is a hidden crisis, driven by low wages in work employment, high care dependency and now rising unemployment. Although very few people in Powys today experience absolute poverty, there are those who fail to achieve the standards of living that we expect in an affluent developed country beyond the basic necessities of life. Energy costs have risen exponentially, the price of diesel has hit an all-time high, but wages are not rising to match this. Latest figures show that the unemployment rate in mid and south west Wales has risen to 3.5 per cent over the year. I visited a job centre in Llandrindod Wells recently, where work coaches told me about the lack of jobs being created in rural areas. So, how is the Cabinet Minister working with other areas of Government to address rural poverty in mid Wales and focus on setting the conditions for rural businesses to thrive and take on new staff?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch yn fawr. I do recognise the specific way that poverty and deprivation can affect rural areas in particular. So, one of the things that I did was make sure that, when I announced funding for local authorities that provides support for wider poverty prevention activities and also emergency food aid, which include those community hubs where preventative services are provided, that funding also included an allocation for rural local authorities, a rural allocation, recognising the added challenges of delivering support in rural areas. That rural premium element has been included on a test-and-learn basis, to recognise the additional challenges, as the Member has outlined, and also the costs that rural local authorities and other services can face when delivering cost-of-living and poverty support.

On your broader question, obviously, a fair and prosperous Wales, the whole of Wales, is the long-term vision of this Government, and it's reasserted in our programme for government. A key part of this vision is to support rural areas by policies across Government designed to bring tangible benefits to our rural communities. Our rural communities are diverse, they have diverse needs, they face challenges due to geography and distance and cost and scalability. And we know about ageing population in rural areas, lack of employment opportunities, lower wages and, of course, infrequent transport provisions. So, we're bringing forward a legislative duty on rural-proofing, and that's expected to bring long-term benefits to rural communities, considering their specific circumstances, and, of course, that is something that will apply across all Government policies.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Mae Llywodraeth Cymru newydd gyhoeddi pecyn o bron i £5 miliwn i gefnogi'r rhai sy'n dioddef tlodi ac i adeiladu gwydnwch ariannol hirdymor ar draws ein cymunedau. Sut fydd y Llywodraeth yn sicrhau bod y cyllid hwn yn cyrraedd y rhai mwyaf bregus, yn enwedig mewn rhannau gwledig o'n hetholaeth ni, Brycheiniog Tawe Nedd? Diolch yn fawr.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: The Welsh Government has just announced a package of almost £5 million to support those experiencing poverty and to build financial resilience in the long term across our communities. How will the Government ensure that this funding reaches the most vulnerable, particularly in rural parts of our constituency of Brycheiniog Tawe Nedd? Thank you.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr i chi am y cwestiwn atodol yna, yn benodol am Frycheiniog Tawe Nedd—mae'n etholaeth, wrth gwrs, dwi'n ei rhannu. Ond, fel y dywedais i, rŷn ni fel Llywodraeth yn hollol benderfynol bod y cymorth rŷn ni'n gallu ei ddarparu, a'r gefnogaeth rŷn ni'n gallu ei darparu, yn cyrraedd y rhai sydd fwyaf mewn angen, gan gynnwys yr aelwydydd hynny sy'n wynebu heriau ychwanegol a chostau ychwanegol sy'n ymwneud â bod yn rhan o ardal wledig, fel y gwnes i osod mas yn fy ateb yn gynharach. Rŷn ni'n credu bod awdurdodau lleol gyda'r wybodaeth a'r ddealltwriaeth orau o ran sut i gefnogi'r cymunedau hynny. Felly, rŷn ni wedi rhoi i'r awdurdodau lleol yna ganllawiau i fynd gyda'r cyllid y gwnaeth yr Aelod gyfeirio ato fe, i sicrhau bod y cyllid yna yn mynd at y rhai sydd ei angen fwyaf, ond hefyd bod gyda nhw ddisgresiwn i ddefnyddio'r cyllid yna ar gyfer y prosiectau a'r cynlluniau fyddai'n cael yr effaith fwyaf. Byddwn ni'n gweithio'n agos nawr gyda'n partneriaid ni i sicrhau ein bod ni'n edrych ar sut y mae'r cyllid yna yn cael effaith, pwy fydd yn cael eu cyrraedd, pa mor effeithiol fydd e, fel roeddwn i'n dweud, gyda'r system brofi a dysgu yna, er mwyn sicrhau bod y cyllid yn cael ei ddefnyddio'n effeithiol.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you very much for that supplementary question, specifically about Brycheiniog Tawe Nedd, which is a constituency, of course, that I share. But, as I said, we as a Government are determined that the support that we can provide does reach those who are most in need, including those households that are facing additional challenges and additional costs related to being part of a rural area, as I set out in my earlier answer. We believe that local authorities have the best understanding and information on how to support those communities. So, we have given those local authorities guidelines to go with the funding that the Member referred to, to ensure that that funding does go to those who need it most, but also that they have some discretion to use that funding for the projects and schemes that would have the biggest impact. We will work closely now with our partners to ensure that we look at how that funding is having an effect, who it reaches, and how effective it will be, as I said, with this test-and-learn system, to ensure that that funding is being used effectively.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 2. Sut y bydd Llywodraeth Cymru yn sicrhau y bydd Dechrau'n Deg a'r cynnig gofal plant newydd 20 awr, gyda'i gilydd, yn ddigon hyblyg i gefnogi bywydau gwaith teuluoedd? OQ64565
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 2. How will the Welsh Government ensure that Flying Start and the new 20-hour childcare offer will together be flexible enough to support families' working lives? OQ64565

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch am y cwestiwn. Mae'n rhaid i'r gofal plant sy'n cael ei ariannu fod yn hyblyg i deuluoedd ac yn realistig hefyd i ddarparwyr. Felly, rŷn ni'n gweithio gydag awdurdodau lleol a darparwyr cofrestredig i ehangu'r ddarpariaeth mewn ffordd gynaliadwy. Bydd symud tuag at 20 awr yr wythnos yn caniatáu sesiynau hirach, mwy hyblyg er mwyn cefnogi rhieni i weithio, hyfforddi neu gynyddu eu horiau.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you for the question. Funded childcare must be flexible for families and deliverable for providers. We are working with local authorities and registered providers to expand provision sustainably. Moving towards 20 hours a week will enable longer, more flexible sessions to support parents to work, train or increase their hours.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch am eich ateb.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you for that response.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Flying Start is a brilliant initiative, despite its flaws. Too many children start nursery with a developmental age of two, while some of the more advanced start with a developmental age approaching four. Some start not toilet trained and with very limited communication and social skills. Flying Start gives an opportunity to narrow that gap and helps build self-esteem so that children start school not as self-defined failures. There have been problems based on the lower super-output areas, where some of the wealthiest in Swansea were in Flying Start areas and some of the poorest were not. Using the Welsh index of multiple deprivation does not work in heterogeneous areas. House prices are a much better indicator. Will the Minister commit to continuing the Flying Start provision and improving on it?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Dwi'n ddiolchgar iawn am y cwestiwn. Dwi'n meddwl eich bod chi wedi rhoi eich bys ar y peth yna, Mike. Hynny yw, rŷn ni wedi cael llythyron gan etholwyr—ac mae e'n dod o bob rhan—ac mae nifer fawr o Aelodau yn y Siambr yn pwysleisio'r pwynt yma, yn croesawu nod y Llywodraeth o ehangu'r ddarpariaeth a sicrhau tegwch, fel ein bod ni'n gallu cyrraedd y plant hynny a'r teuluoedd hynny sydd ar hyn o bryd ddim yn cael eu cyrraedd gan y model presennol. Rŷn ni hefyd yn gwybod bod y model yn un cymhleth a bod pobl weithiau yn colli mas ar gefnogaeth, ond hefyd rhai eraill ddim yn gallu mynd at y gefnogaeth hynny oherwydd y model daearyddol. Rwy'n falch iawn, yn Abertawe, fod y sir eisoes wedi cyflwyno cam cyntaf y gofal plant sy'n cael ei ariannu gan Lywodraeth Cymru ar gyfer pob plentyn dwy flwydd oed, 12.5 awr, ac felly fe fyddwn ni nawr yn symud at y cam nesaf yna o ddarparu mwy o oriau yr wythnos, gan hefyd sicrhau ein bod ni'n adeiladu ar yr ymyriadau hynod o bwysig a gwerthfawr yna i'r teuluoedd sydd fwyaf mewn angen.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: I'm extremely grateful for that question. I think you've put your finger on it there, Mike. We have received letters from constituents—and this comes from all areas—and many Members of the Chamber have also emphasised that very point, welcoming the Government's objective of expanding provision and ensuring fairness, so that we can reach those children and families who, at the moment, aren't reached by the current model. We also know that the model is a complex one, and that people sometimes lose out on support, but others can't even access the support because of that geographical model. I am very pleased that, in Swansea, the county has already introduced the first phase of the funded childcare provided by the Welsh Government for all children of two years of age, at 12.5 hours, and so we will move now to that next step of providing more hours a week, thereby ensuring that we do build on those very important and valuable interventions for those families most in need.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: It's encouraging that the Plaid Cymru Welsh Government is on track to deliver 12.5 hours of funded childcare per week across all 22 local authorities by the end of the financial year, a commitment that Welsh Labour promised but failed to deliver in its last five-year term in Government. Ashamedly, poverty has seeped throughout our nation. Whilst Flying Start was a good starting point, the Bevan Foundation warned that relying on this framework risks unequal access and lacks the flexibility that parents need. The phrase 'postcode lottery' has become synonymous with Flying Start. Tackling poverty and inequality requires decisive action. This is why people voted for Plaid Cymru. We have a vision for childcare that actually works for families and puts money back in their pockets, when the average weekly cost of a childcare place in Wales is £290 a week, £58 more a week than in England. Will the Cabinet Minister provide more information on the timeline for rolling out the remainder of the offer and what steps are being taken to ensure equal access to the universal childcare that will tackle the cost of living?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch yn fawr, a dwi'n cydnabod hefyd yr ymgyrchu mae'r Aelod wedi'i wneud ar y cwestiwn o ran argaeledd a chost gofal plant, ac effaith hynny nid yn unig ar deuluoedd mewn tlodi, ond hefyd o ran anghydraddoldeb rhywedd sy'n effeithio'n bennaf, wrth gwrs, ar fenywod.

Felly, fe wnaethoch chi sôn yn fanna am ddadansoddiad Sefydliad Bevan ynglŷn â'r model newydd a ddylai fod, neu'r model gorau a all fod, ar gyfer darparu gofal plant i bawb mewn ffordd sydd yn deg ac yn cyrraedd y nod. Dwi'n cytuno gyda hynny—bod yna heriau ac mae yna benderfyniadau pwysig sydd angen eu gwneud—ond hefyd fod yna, fel y mae Sefydliad Bevan wedi tanlinellu, gyfle nawr i wneud pethau'n wahanol ac yn well. Dwi'n cytuno bod y system ar hyn o bryd yn rhy gymhleth ac yn rhy gostus, felly hyn sydd wrth waelod ein rhaglen ni ar gyfer datblygu ac ehangu a gwneud yn siŵr bod y system sydd gyda ni yn esblygu er gwell.

Felly, dwi'n meddwl, o ran yr amserlen, y byddwch chi'n gwybod ein bod ni wedi sôn am gymryd proses gam wrth gam. Mae hynny'n hanfodol er mwyn sicrhau ein bod ni'n gwneud hyn mewn ffordd sy'n gynaliadwy ac yn cymryd i ystyriaeth anghenion rhieni a darparwyr. Felly, fe fyddaf i yn gallu rhoi—. Rŷn ni wedi gweld cynnydd gwych ar hyn o bryd, fel gwnaeth yr Aelod sôn. Fe fyddwn ni'n gallu dweud erbyn diwedd y flwyddyn ariannol yma—felly, llai na blwyddyn o oes y Llywodraeth yma—y bydd pob plentyn dwy flywydd oed yn gallu cael cynnig o ofal plant ble bynnag maen nhw'n byw o 12.5 awr, ac fe fyddaf i'n diweddaru'r Senedd yn nes ymlaen y tymor hwn, siŵr o fod ar ddechrau Rhagfyr, ynglŷn â beth fydd y camau nesaf.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Thank you, and I recognise as well the campaigning that the Member has done on the availability and cost of childcare and the effect of that not only on families in poverty, but also in terms of gender inequality that affects women mostly.

You mentioned the analysis made by the Bevan Foundation in terms of the new model that should, or the best model that could, provide childcare to all in a way that is fair and reaches the aim. I agree with that—that there are challenges and important decisions that need to be made—but also, as the Bevan Foundation has underlined, that there is an opportunity now to do things differently and better. I agree that the system currently is too complex and too costly, and that's at the heart of our programme for developing and expanding and making sure that the system we have evolves for the better.

So, I think, in terms of the timetable, you'll know that we have spoken about taking a step-by-step approach that's essential to ensure that we do this in a sustainable manner and that takes into consideration the needs of providers and parents. Therefore, I will be able to—. And we have seen excellent progress, as the Member mentioned. We will be able to say by the end of this financial year—so, in less than a year of this Government's time—that every two-year-old child can be offered childcare wherever they live of 12.5 hours, and I will update the Senedd later on this term, probably at the beginning of December, as to what the next steps will be.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: We are all aware that Flying Start has some limitations. Its delivery can vary between local authorities and some families are left out, but the figures also show that the programme is one that families are using. So, in 2025-26, 98.5 per cent of eligible children were offered Flying Start childcare, with 85.4 per cent taking up that offer. The programme also delivered 211,000 health contacts to families across Wales. I'm concerned that, in moving towards a universal offer, we could lose sight of the targeted support that Flying Start provides to some of Wales's most disadvantaged families. Flying Start is more than childcare. It provides health visiting, parental support and help with speech, language and communication. So, will the Government give this Senedd a clear guarantee that, as the universal childcare offer expands, families currently benefiting from the wider Flying Start package will not lose vital services or see them diluted? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I can absolutely give you that guarantee. Obviously, we do see a lot of families taking up the Flying Start offer, but, because it's limited geographically, there are many families, especially, we know, and there are more children in poverty who live outside Flying Start areas than actually live within Flying Start areas. So, this is why we're getting to grips with this model, because it isn't as effective as it could be.

This is a Government that has prevention at its heart in everything we do, and we absolutely recognise the contribution that the other elements, besides childcare, of Flying Start can provide. So, we recognise the huge contribution that that workforce, specifically on the non-childcare elements of Flying Start, provide and the importance of their work. So, the end goal is a childcare and an early years system that includes that preventative element that is easier for families to navigate and is clearer for partners to deliver, and is better able to support all children who need that intervention.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: I now call on the party spokespeople to question the Cabinet Minister. The Reform UK spokesperson, Cristiana Emsley.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Ddirprwy Lywydd. Deputy First Minister, I want to put you on notice from the outset: my questions today will be direct, so I respectfully ask you to address the questions rather than the person asking them.

In June, I wrote to you asking seven specific questions about the implementation and protection of women's sex-based rights in Wales. For the first time, I'm making that correspondence public. I asked what action your Government would take, what timetable you would follow, what instruction would be issued to public bodies, how women's sex-based rights would be protected in practice, and whether existing Government policies and guidance would be reviewed. You answered none of those seven questions directly. You are the Cabinet Minister responsible for equality and human rights. More than three months later, women are entitled to something more than general assurances. Women do not need another statement of principle; they need implementation. So, I'll ask you again: what has your Government actually done to implement women's sex-based rights in Wales? What has changed? What instructions have been issued? And by what date can women expect those rights to be protected consistently in practice?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch am y cwestiwn.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you for the question.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I think there's a fundamental misunderstanding here. The Equality and Human Rights Commission's code of practice for services, public functions and associations, which came into force on 5 August, means that we have to comply with our legal duties as a Government in respect of the Equality Act 2010. All bodies and service providers must themselves ensure that they're complying with the law. The Welsh Government of course expects all organisations to comply with the law, and we've clearly stated that. But the application then means careful consideration of the guidance in each situation. It is the responsibility of all the bodies and service providers to do that. The EHRC is the regulator to ensure that that is happening. They are responsible for monitoring compliance with equality and human rights law, ensuring that public authorities and other duty bearers meet their obligations. That isn't a responsibility of the Government.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I'm sticking to the parliamentary code of practice, so I can't answer back. 

Deputy First Minister, in June, when I scrutinised the cost of your childcare—

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: You can. You can use your second question to do that.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: No, I've got a lot to go through today, but the law is the law and the judgment was issued on 16 July. So, hiding behind the EHRC is not going to cut it. [Interruption.] Shall I carry on with the second question?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Perhaps you can write to the EHRC to get clarity.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
In July, when I scrutinised the cost of your childcare commitment, you told this Chamber that my questioning baffled you. You even suggested that I should do a little bit of reading. Well, I remain baffled by your bafflement, because scrutiny eventually extracted something rather important. Your £375 million mid point became a potential funding range of £250 million to £500 million a year. I would be delighted to do a little bit more reading if your Government would finally publish the numbers. 

Deputy First Minister, let us leave the personal remarks behind and deal with the maths. What is your Government's latest fully modelled annual cost of delivering this commitment? What provisions are you asking the finance Minister to make in the forthcoming budget? What measurable benchmarks will you use to demonstrate that hundreds of millions of pounds of taxpayers' money has delivered the promised outcomes? Because the budget cannot be baffled by the maths and eventually the numbers have to add up.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
The figures will become clear in the forthcoming draft budget. You will be able to scrutinise that, the committees will be able to scrutinise that, and, of course, questions can be asked here of Ministers around their spending plans. 

You're asking about progress. In terms of the money that we've already spent, you'll know that there was £55 million in total allocated in the supplementary budget, which we have put to work in terms of expanding childcare and also with some capital grants to enable that to happen. So, 78.9 per cent of all two-year-olds are now offered childcare. Over 13,000 new two-year-olds have been offered a childcare place. Over 9,900 new two-year-olds attended their funded childcare, and over 2,000 of those children attended funded childcare in a Welsh-medium setting. 

As I said, we are now expecting, and I've had assurances from local authorities—. Many Members in the Chamber will probably see this happening now—their local authorities putting out that offer to parents of that age group. That's happening progressively in the way that we said it would. And then, by the end of the financial year, all two-year-olds in Wales, in every single local authority, will be offered 12.5 hours of funded childcare. I think there are quite a lot of statistics there for you.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Deputy First Minister, I have another piece of correspondence that I'm making public for the first time today: our exchange about the veterans and armed forces covenant. In June, I asked you for something very simple, namely measurable outcomes—has veteran homelessness fallen, have healthcare waiting times improved, are veterans finding employment more successfully, and are they accessing housing more quickly. Your response listed programmes, pathways, meetings and future work, but, Deputy First Minister, an activity is not an outcome. A programme existing is not evidence that it is working.

You told me that specific performance measures were something you were planning to raise with the UK Government, that the UK veterans strategy offered a potential way forward, and that further measures would be explored. We are now several months further on, so I'm asking you again: can you give this Senedd just one measurable outcome showing that veterans in Wales are materially better off because of the armed forces covenant on housing, homelessness, healthcare or employment? Will you now commit to publishing Welsh performance measures against which you, as the Minister responsible, can actually be held accountable?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch am y cwestiwn.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you for the question.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
We are of course, as I'll reiterate again, absolutely committed to upholding the principles of the armed forces covenant, ensuring fair access to healthcare, housing, employment, education, skills and training for veterans and their families. The covenant is absolutely a social justice issue, reducing the potential for disadvantage from serving in the armed forces. By and large, service in the armed forces does lead to positive outcomes. I have submitted a legislative consent memorandum to the Senedd in respect of the Armed Forces Bill, including its plans for broadening the armed forces covenant.

The covenant, of course, doesn't specify outcomes or targets. It's about consideration. It's about understanding why there needs to be a specific way of working, to be adapted insofar as the services that veterans may come in contact with, to reduce that disadvantage and to afford a special consideration. It's clear that plans for broadening the armed forces covenant will impact the way we work, and so we need to consider policy now across a broad range of areas through that armed forces lens. We already have the ways and means to do that in other areas, of course, through our integrated impact assessment process.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Llefarydd Llafur Cymru, Lynne Neagle.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Welsh Labour spokesperson, Lynne Neagle.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Ddirprwy Lywydd. I'd like to return to Flying Start. The First Minister said in response to my colleague Ken Skates yesterday that she wants to build on Flying Start and make it available everywhere. But as I said to you, and as we've heard previously today, Flying Start is so much more than childcare. It is that enhanced health visiting, speech and language, and parenting support. I would argue that that focus on strong parent-infant relationships is one of the most defining things you can do to transform lifelong good mental health from babies growing into adults.

The letter that went out from the Welsh Government to local authorities asking them not to use the term ‘Flying Start’ to describe Flying Start childcare has caused some concern. Indeed, there have been some suggestions, which I hope aren't true, that different local authorities have received different letters. I will ask you today: will you publish the letter that has gone to local authorities so that Senedd Members can understand what local authorities are being told about Flying Start?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I just want to reflect first of all that there seems to be the suggestion that there's some kind of malign motivation behind the fact that we want to evolve this model, and there absolutely isn't. Local authorities, of course, have been engaged with us from the very beginning. There’s a WLGA representative on the expert group, and has been from the early days of this Government, because we started work on this commitment, as you would expect, immediately after the Cabinet was formed. They have always been fully in the loop.

As regards the moving away from that model, that's absolutely not what this is about. It's about evolving what it is. The main reason why we want to call something Welsh Government-funded childcare is for the very reason, as I outlined earlier, that people, now we’re making a universal offer, don't think they're eligible, because they're so used to the Flying Start geographical cliff edge that means that somebody in one street is eligible and somebody on the other street isn't. So, what we wanted to do in the promotion of our rolling out of universal childcare is make that clear. That was the sole motivation: it was a communication to make it clear to parents that they were now eligible for that universal offer.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you for that clarification. I think it would be useful if you could commit to publishing the letter for transparency. I don't think anybody is suggesting malign intent; I and others are worried about a programme that provides a package of support for babies at a really critical time in their lives. You've talked about evolving the programme, and I recognise what's been said about the number of children living in poverty that aren't able to access it, but, for me, the solution to that is to look at how it's delivered, rather than to alter the four-element basis of Flying Start. When you talk about evolving Flying Start, is it your intention to offer that range of services to more children by looking at how that is delivered? What assurance can you give that nobody who is receiving that service now will lose it, and that, actually, more people will have the opportunity to access that range of support in that critical first 1,000 days?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: That is absolutely our intention. You will know, as the former Chair—. I think you conducted an inquiry when you were Chair of the Children, Young People and Education Committee in the Senedd before last. I think you did an inquiry on outreach and on how that approach wasn't reaching all those in need. So, I know that you understand this well. We've used that Flying Start model as the current vehicle for the first phase of our expansion of childcare, but, of course, we have to make sure that the support that is available is available for all children, for all the reasons that your committee inquiry pointed out. At the same time as delivering that universal childcare offer, we have to look at options to enhance the early years support that we're providing, to make sure it does get to all those children. The majority of children in poverty in Wales do not live in Flying Start areas, and therefore are not able to avail themselves of it. When I say 'enhance', that would mean that the children within those Flying Start areas who are currently receiving that support absolutely will not be losing out.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Llefarydd y Ceidwadwyr Cymreig, Natasha Asghar.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Welsh Conservative spokesperson, Natasha Asghar.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you so much, Deputy Presiding Officer. Cabinet Minister, many households across Wales are struggling with rising living costs, yet too often the response from your Welsh Government is to request more powers and expand dependency, rather than creating opportunity. Recent debates around welfare reform and our ballooning benefit bill have highlighted the need to ensure that support reaches those who genuinely need it, whilst also helping others into sustainable employment. At the same time, Wales continues to have some of the lowest wages and highest levels of economic inactivity in the United Kingdom.

My Welsh Conservative colleagues and I argue the best route out of poverty is through lower taxes, economic growth and job creation, not an ever-growing reliance on the welfare state. Cabinet Minister, what assessment has the Plaid Cymru Government made of whether your anti-poverty policies are actually reducing long-term welfare dependency rather than simply managing or, at worst, masking the symptoms of poverty? Thank you.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch. The Member is absolutely right as regards economic prosperity. Making sure that we have well-paid jobs and jobs that pay fairly and have fair work conditions is absolutely key to making sure that we can lift families out of poverty. But I do reject the narrative around dependency on benefits. People are eligible for those benefits because their income is currently not sufficient to make sure that they are able to live with dignity and meet their essential needs. I think there is a fundamental difference of values and principles between us on this. We will absolutely make sure that every penny that this Government spends—and, obviously, the Member knows that welfare policy is not devolved to Wales—goes to those who most need that support. And of course, we will not be quibbling about who is eligible for that support. If they are in need, if they are in poverty, if they are disabled and need our help, then we will help them.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you for that response, Cabinet Minister. Tackling child poverty is one of your Government's key stated priorities. However, despite nearly three decades of Labour-led Governments here in Wales, some that your party even helped prop up, too many families remain dependent on benefits, foodbanks and emergency support. Your own portfolio includes responsibility for co-ordinating measures to tackle child poverty and engagement with UK Government on such matters. Yet many working families tell us that what they need is not another strategy or warm words—they need better paying jobs, affordable childcare and stronger economic growth.

The Welsh Conservatives have proposed such measures by extending free childcare, reducing the tax burden on working households to ensure that they keep more of what they earn, whilst also calling for a dedicated poverty action plan, focusing on children and fuel poverty. Given the continued rise in reliance on the welfare state amongst many Welsh households, can you, Cabinet Minister, explain how your Government's approach differs from treating poverty after it occurs, instead of addressing the actual cause that keeps families trapped with it in the first place?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Well, I'm glad that you agree with me and I hope you were listening carefully to the action we are taking on affordable childcare. That's why it's one of our main priorities as a Government and one of the main policies that, of course, I'm working on. It's a transformational, complex policy, but we absolutely know that it is fundamental to making sure that we can make those costs less for families and also give them the opportunity to be able to get back into the labour market and also increase their hours and get back into training and education.

On the point on how we're doing things differently, well, I have already said and set out, and reiterated this in my scrutiny session in committee last week, that I am not going to be throwing the baby out with the bath water as regards the child poverty strategy. But I do think that it needs a tighter focus and I do think that it needs measurable targets and milestones for us to make sure that what we are doing is having the desired effect and the intended effect.

So, I have already started work on developing and focusing in on what that more honed child poverty strategy can look like, and, as I said, including thinking about how we can evaluate as we go along, making sure we measure our progress. So, we will be working on that, we're developing it with stakeholders, considering, then, how to report on that progress to show what impact we are having. And I've already met with our external reference group and I've also met across Cabinet as well. We've got a cross-Cabinet taskforce on this very issue to make sure that we are aligned on our ambitions for that strategy and the types of targets we think will be useful to guide our work.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 3. A wnaiff y Gweinidog Cabinet roi diweddariad ar gyflwyno cynnig gofal plant Llywodraeth Cymru ym Mhowys? OQ64599
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 3. Will the Cabinet Minister provide an update on the roll-out of the Welsh Government’s childcare offer in Powys? OQ64599

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr am y cwestiwn. Gan ddefnyddio'r cyllid ychwanegol y gwnaethon ni ei gyhoeddi yn gynharach eleni, rwyf wrth fy modd bod Powys yn gallu cyflwyno cam cyntaf y cynnig gofal plant a ariennir gan y Llywodraeth o 12.5 awr o ofal o ansawdd i bob plentyn dwy oed o fis Ionawr 2027.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you very much for the question. Using the additional funding we announced earlier this year, I am delighted that Powys is able to roll out the first phase of the Government funded childcare offer of 12.5 hours of quality childcare for all two-year-olds from January 2027.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr am y diweddariad positif yna. Mae gwastad yn bryder yn y canolbarth fod pob dim yn mynd i'r ardaloedd trefol neu ddinesig. Byddai cael sicrwydd, felly, bydd ein hardaloedd gwledig yr un mor gymwys ac yn elwa o'r datblygiad pwysig yma ym maes gofal plant yn cael ei werthfawrogi. Diolch yn fawr.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you very much for that positive update. There is always a concern in mid Wales that everything goes to urban or city areas. An assurance, therefore, that our rural areas will also benefit from this important development in childcare would be appreciated. Thank you very much.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch. Ie, mae gofal plant hyblyg yn hanfodol, dwi'n meddwl, er mwyn cefnogi teuluoedd gyda chostau byw, a hynny ar draws Cymru ac ar draws pob ardal, er mwyn galluogi rhieni, fel roeddwn i'n sôn, i fanteisio ar fwy o gyfleoedd i weithio, i astudio, neu gynyddu eu horiau nhw, ac, wrth gwrs, er mwyn rhoi'r dechrau gorau hefyd i bob plentyn. Felly, rŷn ni'n datblygu'r cynnig gofal plant yna, a'r flaenoriaeth, fel roeddwn i'n sôn, oedd cynnig y 12.5 awr yma i bob plentyn ar draws Cymru—ac mae Powys yn dangos eu bod nhw'n mynd i fod yn gwneud cynnydd ar hynny yn fuan iawn, felly, dwi wrth fy modd. Ac mae disgwyl i'r system geisiadau yna agor i bob teulu ym Mhowys erbyn diwedd Tachwedd.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you. Yes, flexible childcare is crucial, I think, in order to support families with the cost of living, across Wales and in every area, in order to enable parents, as I mentioned, to take up more opportunities to work, to study or to increase their hours, and, of course, to give the best possible start to every child too. So, we are developing that childcare offer, and the priority, as I mentioned, was the offer of 12.5 hours for all children across Wales—and Powys has demonstrated that they will be making progress on that very soon, so I am delighted. And the applications system is expected to open to all families in Powys by the end of November.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you, Cabinet Minister. I welcome the principle of extending childcare, but there does seem to be a rather large gap between announcing an entitlement and families actually benefiting from it. Powys County Council has itself estimated that the parents of more than 1,000 young children in the county could be missing out on free or reduced-cost childcare. And, of course, in a county as large and rural as Powys, eligibility is only half the issue. There also has to be a suitable provider within a reasonable distance of where a family lives. So, Cabinet Minister, as you roll out this offer, what are you doing to ensure that Powys County Council not only identifies those families who are entitled to support, but has sufficient childcare provision for them actually to use it?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr iawn am y cwestiwn atodol yna.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you very much for that supplementary question.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: We are committed to ensuring that childcare expansion works for families in all parts of Wales, and that's including rural communities, where provision can be more dispersed and can be more fragile. So, we already have some flexibility in the system through guidance, through funding and local authority planning. But we are, as a part of this expansion programme, actively looking at what more can be done to ensure childcare hours and transport solutions and capital investment all respond to the specific needs of rural communities. So, local authorities use childcare sufficiency assessments and annual action plans to identify those gaps in provision, including those rural challenges, and we continue to support practical solutions, then, such as co-locations with schools and community hubs. We also recognise that childminders are really important as well in rural communities, and so we're working with partners, including Cwlwm, to support workforce development, business sustainability and provider capacity.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Swyddfa Bost Caerffili
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Caerphilly Post Office

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 4. Pa asesiad y mae'r Gweinidog Cabinet wedi'i wneud o effaith cau swyddfa bost Caerffili? OQ64598
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 4. What assessment has the Cabinet Minister made of the impact of the closure of Caerphilly post office? OQ64598

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Mae gwasanaethau swyddfeydd post yn chwarae rôl hanfodol wrth gefnogi cymunedau. Mae'r materion hyn, wrth gwrs, wedi'u cadw'n ôl o fewn cylch cyfrifoldeb Llywodraeth y Deyrnas Gyfunol, ac mae'r Llywodraeth honno wedi datgan mai ei nod yw cadw cymaint o ganghennau a gwasanaethau â phosibl.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Post office services play a vital role in supporting communities. These matters, of course, are reserved and are the responsibility of the UK Government, and that Government has stated that their aim is to retain as many branches and services as possible.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Minister, can I thank you for your response? I, along with the leader of Caerphilly County Borough Council, have taken part in direct meetings with the Post Office to secure a suitable replacement in the town centre, but we are encountering a wall of excuses. The reason given by the Post Office as to why alternative sites are unsuitable do not stack up, because the excuse is that they are simply unsuitable—one site, across the road from the post office that had been there, to my knowledge, for at least 73 years, was because there is unsuitable parking. Minister, can I please ask you if you could commit to making direct representations to the Post Office executive to challenge these reasons for site rejections? We do need transparency on when the town centre will finally get its service back. I do feel that if the local Senedd Member—sorry, one of the local Senedd Members—and the leader of council can't get answers, I'm sure, they may listen to you, Minister. I know that I certainly would. [Laughter.]

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch, Lindsay, am y cwestiwn. Yn gyntaf oll, rwy'n moyn cydnabod y pryder pan fo cymuned yn colli gwasanaethau. Dwi'n gwybod bod nifer ohonom ni wedi gweld hyn yn ein cymunedau dros y blynyddoedd, ar y stryd fawr o ran banciau yn benodol, ac, yn yr un modd, weithiau, pan fo gwasanaeth post yn dod i ben.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you, Lindsay, for the question. First of all, I want to acknowledge the concern when a community loses services. I know a number of us have seen this in our communities over the years, on the high street in terms of banks specifically, and, in the same way, sometimes, when post office services come to an end.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I just want to let the Member know that I actually met with the Post Office, with Post Office Ltd, yesterday. Again, as I said, they provided reassurance to maintain the network, as is their duty. I'm pleased to say that the Post Office Ltd confirmed to me that they have—because I did raise this topic specifically around post office services in Caerphilly—received expressions of interest to run the post office service in Caerphilly, and these are now currently being reviewed. So, that process, from expressions of interest to being, typically, open, takes up to six months. So, I hope that that will give your constituents assurance that we, hopefully, will see that post office service resume in your area.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I thank the Minister for the answer there. The other concern that people are passing to me in terms of post office closures—whether it's Caerphilly or throughout the constituency—is, once the post office closes, it's the lack of being able to get ID, identification; it's the additional services that the post office uniquely provides to communities. I appreciate what you said on Caerphilly there, but what about other parts of Wales and my constituency that have lost that service, and now people are unable to get identification, because of simple things like the proofreading, the assistance, that the post office provides? What help can the Welsh Government provide to constituents there?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Rwy'n cydnabod yn llwyr y gofidiau yma. Dwi'n siŵr, eto, eu bod nhw'n gyfarwydd i ni i gyd. Mae'r gwasanaethau yn rhai hanfodol iawn i'n cymunedau ni, yn enwedig i bobl sydd, efallai, ddim yn medru defnyddio, neu does yna ddim argaeledd, trafnidiaeth gyhoeddus ac yn y blaen, er mwyn mynd i'r dref nesaf. Maen nhw'n rhan bwysig o'n canol trefi a'n strydoedd mawr, a dyna yw safbwynt y Llywodraeth, yn sicr.

Wrth gwrs, eto, dyw materion sy'n ymwneud â swyddfeydd post ddim wedi eu datganoli i Weinidogion Cymru. Fel y soniais i yn yr ateb cynharach, mae ymrwymiad Llywodraeth y Deyrnas Gyfunol i swyddfeydd post yn cynnwys cynlluniau i gadw maint y rhwydwaith fel y mae, ac mae hynny'n golygu chwilio wedyn am fusnesau newydd i gynnig y gwasanaeth pan fydd swyddfeydd post unigol yn cau. Ond mae hefyd yn cynnwys ymrwymiad i leoli swyddfeydd post yng nghanol trefi, lle y bo'n bosibl. Achos, fel roeddwn i'n dweud, dwi'n cytuno—rŷn ni'n gwybod, onid ydyn ni, fod presenoldeb swyddfa bost yn cynyddu nifer yr ymwelwyr â stryd fawr, yn ogystal, wrth gwrs, â darparu'r gwasanaethau hanfodol yna.

Mae ein rhaglen lywodraethu ni yn cynnwys ymrwymiad i archwilio'r opsiynau yna i adfywio canol ein trefi, felly, wrth gwrs yn gysylltiedig â'n gwaith ni o ran y tasglu canol trefi rŷn ni wedi ei sefydlu. Felly, dwi'n siŵr y byddai sicrhau bod swyddfeydd post yn gallu bod yn rhan o strydoedd mawr bywiog yn gallu bod yn rhan o'r gwaith yna.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
I fully recognise those concerns. I'm sure that they are familiar to us all. Those services are crucial to our communities, particularly for people who perhaps can't use public transport or there is no transport available to take them to the next town. They are an important part of our town centres and high streets, and that is the Government's view, most certainly.

But, again, issues related to post offices are not devolved to Welsh Ministers. As I mentioned in an earlier response, the UK Government's commitment to post offices includes plans to retain the size of the network as it is, and that means looking for new businesses to offer those services when individual post offices close. But it also includes a commitment to locate post offices in town centres, where possible. Because, as I said, I agree—we know that post offices increase the number of visitors to the high street, as well as providing those crucial services.

Our programme for government does include a commitment to look at those options to rejuvenate our town centres, and that links to our work in terms of the town-centre taskforce that we've established. So, I'm sure that ensuring that post offices can be part of vibrant high streets could be part of that work too.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Child Poverty

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 5. Beth mae'r Gweinidog Cabinet yn ei wneud i fynd i'r afael â'r heriau gwledig unigryw sy'n gysylltiedig â thlodi plant yng Ngheredigion Penfro? OQ64603
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 5. What is the Cabinet Minister doing to tackle the unique rural challenges associated with child poverty in Ceredigion Penfro? OQ64603

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Rŷn ni'n cydnabod bod teuluoedd mewn ardaloedd gwledig yn gallu wynebu rhwystrau ychwanegol, gan gynnwys mynediad mwy cyfyngedig at gyflogaeth, gwasanaethau a thrafnidiaeth, ynghyd â chostau uwch. Dyna pam mae ein rhaglen lywodraethu yn cynnwys ymrwymiad i ddeddfu ar gyfer prawfesur gwledig, er mwyn helpu i sicrhau canlyniadau gwell i blant sy'n byw mewn tlodi mewn ardaloedd gwledig.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: We recognise that rural families can face additional barriers, including restricted access to employment, services and transport, as well as higher costs. That is why our programme for government includes a commitment to legislate for rural-proofing, helping to deliver better outcomes for children living in poverty in rural areas.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Cabinet Minister. A 2023 report by the Bevan Foundation found that Ceredigion ranks second in child poverty levels across Wales, with Pembrokeshire not far behind. Crisis has also highlighted that many families in my constituency face significant gaps between their incomes and essential living costs, leaving them at greater risk of poverty and financial hardship.

Whilst child poverty exists across Wales, it's often less visible in rural and coastal constituencies. One example in my constituency is Aberporth, a beautiful and vibrant village that many Members might know as a holiday destination, but also where one in four children live in poverty. In these communities, community action can make a real difference to people's lives—for example, the incredible range of activities that are run from the renovated Aberporth village hall that provide not just practical support, but friendships and social support that are invaluable to people.

So, will the Cabinet Minister consider what more can be done to strengthen our community infrastructure as part of your efforts to address child poverty?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch yn fawr. Dwi'n meddwl bod defnyddio'r enghraifft yna y gwnaethoch chi ddefnyddio fanna o ran Aberporth, rhywle dwi'n siŵr bod nifer ohonom ni wedi ymweld ag e—lle hyfryd, lle mor bert, ond mae yna rywbeth cudd, yntefe? Ac mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn cydnabod bod tlodi gwledig yn aml yn llai gweladwy na thlodi sydd yn ein trefi a'n dinasoedd ni, ond dyw e ddim yn llai real. Rŷn ni'n benderfynol fel Llywodraeth o sicrhau bod plant a theuluoedd mewn cymunedau gwledig yn cael y cymorth sydd ei angen arnynt.

Dylai pob plentyn yng Nghymru, lle bynnag maen nhw'n byw, gael yr un cyfle i lwyddo. Felly, rŷn ni eisiau sicrhau bod ein hymrwymiad o ran ein polisïau yn arddangos hynny, a'n bod ni'n cymryd hynny i ystyriaeth ym mhopeth rŷn ni'n ei wneud. Felly, rŷn ni'n cydnabod bod llawer o deuluoedd yn wynebu heriau penodol, fel rydw i wedi sôn yn gynharach, o ran enillion is a chostau teithio ac ynni uwch, ac yn y blaen, ac mae'n anodd hefyd weithiau cael mynediad at y gwasanaethau a'r cymorth maen nhw eu hangen.

Felly, dyna pam rŷn ni wedi sicrhau y cymorth yma i deuluoedd ledled Cymru yn ein pecyn cymorth trechu tlodi, sydd yn werth bron £5 miliwn, sy'n cynnwys y cymorth penodol yna i gymunedau gwledig a chanolfannau, fel yr oedd yr Aelod yn sôn amdanynt, i gynllunio a helpu'r rhai sy'n wynebu'r pwysau ariannol mwyaf.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Thank you very much. I think that using that example you used there in terms of Aberporth, somewhere that I'm sure a number of us have visited—a very beautiful place, a pretty place, but there is something hidden, isn't there? And Welsh Government recognises that rural poverty quite often is less visible than poverty in our towns and cities, but it's no less real. We are determined as a Government to ensure that children and families in rural communities have the support they need.

Every child in Wales, wherever they may live, should have the same opportunity to succeed. So, we want to ensure that our commitment in terms of our policies shows that, and that we take that into consideration in everything that we do. So, we recognise that many families are facing specific challenges, as I've mentioned earlier, in terms of lower pay and higher transport and energy costs, and so on, and also sometimes it's difficult to access the services and support they require.

So, that's why we have ensured that support is available to families throughout Wales in our tackling poverty programme, which is worth about £5 million and includes that specific support for rural communities and centres, such as the Member mentioned, to plan and to help those who are facing the greatest financial pressures.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you to Anna for the question. Deputy First Minister, on 22 September the First Minister told the Senedd that Cynnal was going to be piloted and it is happening, yet your programme for government says that you will 'seek to' pilot Cynnal. The distinction there really matters, Minister, because 'we're going to' is a commitment, while 'seek to' is not. So, for families in Ceredigion Penfro, I have two straightforward questions: will Ceredigion Penfro be included in the Cynnal pilot? And on your childcare commitment, on what date will families in Ceredigion Penfro be able to access the allocated funded hours per week? Families need to know not just what this Government intends to do, but when they will actually receive the support. Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch am y cwestiwn.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you for the question.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I'd like to clarify the reason why it says 'seek to pilot': it's because there's a very important decision that needs to be made by the UK Treasury, because what we don't want to do with Cynnal is make families worse off. We want to make them better off. So, that means the UK Treasury has to give a benefit and tax disregard. We heard some encouraging signs in an interview with Andy Burnham during the Labour conference on that. It's something, of course, that I've been pressing on with the UK Treasury, and so of course has the Cabinet Minister for Finance, because we want them to allow us to—. We have the powers to pilot the payment, but what we don't have are the powers over that tax and benefit disregard. So, that's why we are saying 'seek to pilot', because we don't have—. We wouldn't want to do something if we didn't have that assurance from UK Treasury that it wouldn't make families worse off. 

We are preparing to implement that pilot. We've commissioned an expert team to help lead on that design, thinking about then, obviously, again, the monitoring and evaluation. We want it to be effective. We've already met four times, and we're meeting again in a few weeks' time. It's been an intense piece of work. It's an intense process because we do want to make sure that we can get this payment out to families—a payment that has proven so successful in Scotland in lowering rates of child poverty—out to children who are in need as soon as we possibly can.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: A'r cwestiwn olaf, cwestiwn 6, Carrie Harper.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: And the final question, question 6, Carrie Harper.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Child Poverty

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 6. Pa gamau y mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn eu cymryd i fynd i'r afael â thlodi plant? OQ64596
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 6. What action is the Welsh Government taking to tackle child poverty? OQ64596

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Tackling child poverty is central to our programme for government. We are already delivering on our commitments on free school meals and the childcare offer, as well as developing our Cynnal child payment. Our new child poverty strategy will include clear, measurable targets to improve outcomes for children and families.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch yn fawr iawn. In my constituency of Fflint Wrecsam, there are currently 12,786 children living in poverty. In Caia Park, where I live, we have one of the highest levels of deprivation, not just in the constituency, but one of the highest levels across Cymru. We all know that children who grow up in poverty are far more likely to find themselves categorised as not in education, employment or training later in life, becoming trapped in a cycle of poverty. It's vital that we break that cycle, isn't it, and ensure that every child gets a fair chance to succeed.

We know that progress is possible. The only nation in the UK where child poverty rates are improving is Scotland. And Scotland acts as an example to all of us in Cymru in terms of what can be achieved when Governments have the tools to do more for their own people. The Scottish child payment and their additional powers on welfare are making a tangible difference there. So, my question in many ways follows on from Paul Marr's, which you very eloquently just answered, in terms of the progress the Government is making in implementing Cynnal, our Welsh child payment pilot, and ensuring that under a Plaid Cymru Government, child poverty statistics finally start moving in the right direction.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch yn fawr am y cwestiwn.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Thank you very much for that question.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
We are, as I said, already making progress on the preparation of that implementation of the Cynnal pilot, the Welsh child payment. We have heard views and evidence on how such a payment could make a real tangible difference to families, so we want to make sure that we design a pilot that can demonstrate that. That expert group I was referring to earlier, which I'm co-chairing with Steffan Evans from the Bevan Foundation, is meeting regularly, as I said, to help with that design, help with the implementation, so it launches on a real sound and evidence-based footing as soon as that preparation is complete.

On the tax and benefit disregards, I met with Baroness Sherlock, who's Minister of State in the Department for Work and Pensions, to discuss our ambitions around child poverty more broadly, and also the Cynnal payment. She has agreed to work with us to explore how we can ensure those payments do not impact on tax and benefits. And also, on the implementation piece, it's around how we can share DWP data as well, for delivery purposes. So, our officials are working together to take this forward.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i’r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog a’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Gyfiawnder Cymdeithasol a Chydraddoldeb
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the Deputy First Minister and Cabinet Minister for Social Justice
