XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Symudwn ymlaen i eitem 2, cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd. Cwestiwn 1, Natasha Asghar.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: We'll move now to item 2, questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability. Question 1, Natasha Asghar.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Mannau Gwyrdd Cymunedol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Community Green Spaces

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 1. Pa gamau mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn eu cymryd i ddiogelu mannau gwyrdd cymunedol yng Nghasnewydd ac Islwyn? OQ64574
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 1. What action is the Welsh Government taking to protect community green spaces in Newport and Islwyn? OQ64574

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Obviously, our community green spaces matter for people, for nature and the places where people live. We are investing in programmes that protect and improve them, including in Newport and Islwyn. I want to build on that work, particularly in communities where access to good-quality green space is most limited.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thanks so much for your response. Cabinet Secretary, over the summer, I met up with a group of residents in Newport who are concerned that they are poised to lose the only community green space in their area, and a plan has been drawn up by Newport City Council. Constituents of mine, particularly dog walkers, children and families, make full use of a parcel of land just off Ruskin Avenue in Rogerstone North, but that could soon come to an end if the local authority rubber-stamps the plan to turn the community green space into an allotment site. To be clear, no-one is against allotment sites or developments, but not only would that take away a vital community asset, it's simply not the right site, with fears about even more traffic in the area, as residents are already experiencing and facing that sort of problem.

Cabinet Minister, more than 200 residents have signed a petition calling for the site in Rogerstone North to be ruled out. I've written to the council myself highlighting the residents' concerns and calling for the site to be dropped, and the decision now rests with the local authority. So, will you join me in putting pressure on Newport council to protect this community green space by removing it from the authority's allotment plans?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you for raising this issue. I am aware, actually, of the concerns that residents have raised on this particular issue. You will also know that this is a matter for Newport City Council; it wouldn't be appropriate for me to intervene in what is and should be a local decision. But I think the wider principle here is important. Communities need both accessible green spaces and opportunities to grow food. But it is important, of course, that those local decisions have to reflect the value that people place on these spaces, and access to nature shouldn't depend, really, on where you live. I want more people to have good-quality green spaces close to home, particularly, as I said in my initial answer, where access is currently poorest.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Minister, Wales needs both renewable energy and secure domestic food production. Welsh planning policy already gives considerable weight to protecting our best and most versatile agricultural land. Can you explain how the protection works alongside the Government's drive for renewable energy, so that we increase green generation without unnecessarily losing our most productive farmland?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you for the question. Obviously it's about striking the right balance, isn't it? We know that there is a demand for energy, we know that there is a demand for food, and consequently there will be, sometimes, conflicting demand for land. The planning system is there to try and protect the integrity of those demands in a way that strikes the right balance. Sometimes, planning authorities get it right, other times, maybe, people will disagree, and that's the nature of the situation that we're facing.

You will know—and I am straying into the territory of other Ministers here—that work is ongoing to look at planning policy, particularly in relation to energy infrastructure. There is also work happening on a new national energy strategy for us here in Wales. I will entrust that work to my Cabinet colleagues, and I am confident that they will get it right and also confident, of course, that all Members here in the Senedd will have an opportunity to scrutinise that when the time is right.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
We are very similar in the questioning, Lyn, so I'll try and skirt around some of the other parts of it.

Cabinet Minister, it's not just community green spaces at risk in Casnewydd, but also agricultural land. Currently, plans see 578 acres of farmland given over to solar development at the Candwr and Craig y Perthi sites. Residents have raised serious concerns about flood risk, traffic, landscape damage and impact on wildlife, including the important lapwing habitat on the Gwent levels, particularly around Bishton, which is their only site. What cumulative assessment has the Government made of the impact that these developments will have on food production, biodiversity and local flood risk? And does the Cabinet Minister believe that removing hundreds of acres of agricultural land is compatible with the Government's stated commitment to food security?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Well, thank you for the question. As you say, it's similar to the question that has been asked, and I feel that the answer may well be similar as well. But it is about striking that balance, I think, and, as I say, the planning system should, when it functions properly, take all of those considerations in the round and, hopefully, bring forward the right balance. But we are looking at planning policy in this energy space and we are working as well on the new energy strategy for Wales, much of which will not only deal with solar, but with the additional infrastructure that goes with some of these projects.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Access to green spaces and nature is so important to our physical and mental well-being. The Road to Nature project in Newport is a great example of what can be done, and the incredible work of the Friends of the Road to Nature group, Newport City Council and the wider community has absolutely transformed what was a real criminal dumping ground for rubbish a few years ago, and that's now a haven for wildlife. Biodiversity is absolutely thriving there, and willow emerald damselflies were recorded for the first time in recent weeks, following the completion of a pond dipping area. This area is a real shining example of a community working together for nature restoration. So, will the Welsh Government commit to supporting and funding more projects like this in Casnewydd Islwyn, as well as other parts of Wales?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you for drawing attention to that particular scheme. I always believe that this kind of work is most effective when you empower local communities to take action like that, and, of course, we have backed that commitment with practical investment through Local Places for Nature, for example, because that scheme alone has created or improved thousands of green spaces and pollinator sites across Wales. In Newport and Caerphilly particularly, 28 community garden packages were delivered in the last year, creating nature gardens, orchards, food-growing areas, but wildlife habitats as well. Another 70 nature gardens are planned by the end of this year.

So, there's a lot happening, backed up by the £16 million that the Government has allocated to Local Places for Nature this year. It's very commendable, the work that's happening, and what we really want to see is how we can replicate that as widely as possible across the whole of Wales.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Effaith Peilonau
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Impact of Pylons

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 2. Pa drafodaethau y mae'r Gweinidog Cabinet wedi'u cael gyda'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Fenter, Cysylltedd ac Ynni am effaith peilonau ar gymunedau gwledig? OQ64568
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 2. What discussions has the Cabinet Minister had with the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy about the impact of pylons on rural communities? OQ64568

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I have regular discussions with my Cabinet colleague. In the coming weeks, I know that the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy will set out our plans to turn our manifesto commitment for the undergrounding of new electricity circuits in Wales into a new planning policy.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Farmers in Carmarthenshire have reported Green GEN Cymru contractors arriving on their land without warning, with one recent incident reportedly requiring police attendance. This is causing real anxiety and frustration among farming families. Will the Minister raise these reports urgently with the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy and stand up within Government for the rural communities affected? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you for drawing our attention to that. I'm always concerned when there are any circumstances that require police attendance and police involvement. There's a certain way of doing things, and I think decent courtesy means that that should always be adhered to. I won't be drawn on commenting on any specifics, because I'm sure you can understand that I'd be straying into difficult territory.

But we do expect all developments planned in Wales to have regard to all relevant planning policy, to be sensitively designed and implemented to avoid and to definitely minimise impacts, at least on communities and the environment, but also to maximise the benefits, because I think there are two sides to this coin. When you get it right, it releases a lot of opportunities economically, et cetera, but when you get it wrong, then those are the risks that sometimes appear.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: What conversations has the Cabinet Minister had regarding the national policy statement for electricity network infrastructure with UK Government Ministers?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Well, that isn't really a role of mine within my portfolio. Clearly, it has a relevance to the energy Minister and it will have a relevance to the planning Minister as well. So, maybe you'd like to direct your question to them when the opportunity arises.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Cwestiynau Heb Rybudd gan Lefarwyr y Pleidiau
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Questions Without Notice from Party Spokespeople

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Galwaf yn awr ar lefarwyr y pleidiau i holi'r Gweinidog Cabinet. Llefarydd Reform UK, Laura Anne Jones.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: I now call on the party spokespeople to question the Cabinet Minster. Reform UK spokesperson, Laura Anne Jones.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Deputy Presiding Officer. Firstly, Minister, I want to say 'diolch' to you too for your recent announcements, finally injecting some common sense into Labour's ridiculously rigid nitrate vulnerable zones rules. It's of course welcome and long overdue, as are advance payments for the basic payment scheme and the sustainable farming scheme after such a difficult summer.

But bringing forward that money does not give farmers a penny more overall, and it does not address the downward trajectory of the basic payment scheme. Lawfully, we are all, of course, aware that you have to bring down BPS payments, but it is in your power, Minister, as to how much. Many are struggling on the 60 per cent of the BPS original 2025 value. Now dropping it to just 40 per cent would literally signal the end of most family farms in Wales. As I am, you must be aware that the majority of the 51 per cent remaining on the BPS are those small family farms that you claim to want to protect. Pushing ahead with this cut, with SFS remaining wholly unsuitable, inflexible and unworkable, is playing literally Russian roulette with their livelihoods. Minister, you need to make the SFS workable, and fast, and you need to put protections in place to help those that remain on the BPS. So, would you consider dropping the BPS by just 1 per cent, as opposed to the further 20 per cent, unless of course you do want to be the Minister responsible for the genuine end of family farms across Wales?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I'm under no illusion about the difficult transition that we're on at the minute, from the legacy BPS programme through to the new sustainable farming scheme. It's a journey that we will continue to travel on. You said that the SFS is wholly inflexible. Well, I'd like to think that some of the decisions and announcements that I've made of late shows that we can make it flexible and more workable for more farmers, so we will continue to do that. I will not entertain dropping the transition by just 1 per cent, but I am of course considering making the SFS truly more accessible to as many farmers as possible.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I hope you're more than considering it because it's absolutely completely unworkable, and you know that as well as I do. Not only is dropping the BPS funding by 1 per cent the right thing to do, but by not doing that and pushing ahead with this 20 per cent cut, you're putting our Welsh heritage, our Welsh culture and Welsh language at risk, as well as our national security. You said all the right things in opposition, Minister, didn't you? But now you seem to be struggling to say them and do them as the Minister. I know you've agreed with me in the past that the BPS trajectory needs to be a much more gradual, tapering trajectory—your words, not mine. Now you're in Government as the Minister able to do this, you're backtracking. You said in black and white in this Chamber that you thought that it should be a more just transition—again, your words. So, tell me: will you do it?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
'Just transition' is exactly what we are trying to achieve here. You say that we've done nothing; we've committed £1 billion over the coming three years to farming to make sure that those farmers who aren't sure about coming on board with the SFS can see that there actually is a quantum of funding there that they can access, that they can utilise, to make their businesses and their farms more resilient. Now, some will choose not to do that and I appreciate that. My job is to make sure that as many people as possible who wish to come on that journey can do so. I'm focused on doing that because that is the just transition that we need to see.

But it isn't only about money as well, of course. We have introduced the review into red tape, which will be, hopefully, a great benefit to farmers who are grappling with the amount of paperwork that they're dealing with. You mentioned the control of agricultural pollution changes. We have been pragmatic, we have been practical, and, where we can do that, we will do that. But, ultimately, we are on this journey transitioning into the sustainable farming scheme and we need to keep our focus on getting there.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Well, you're putting family farms in Wales at risk, Minister, by saying that. I hope that you do recognise that, currently, on the SFS, people cannot get on it whether they want to or not.

I'd like to bring back to what Sarah Edwards, one of my colleagues, has just asked you in the Chamber. I, too, am aware of the extremely worrying circumstance that Green GEN Cymru surveyors appear to be arriving unannounced on farms to survey land, with huge machinery, and, not only that, they are not even adhering to their own biosecurity measures, with no checks in place to ensure that they are. This is genuinely concerning. This is not about whether you agree with windfarms or not, Minister. Most of these farms have had bovine TB or are at high risk of it. This is not a theoretical concern either; the High Court has already found Green GEN lacking in terms of their biosecurity measures. Without the right measures in place here, there is a real risk of disease like TB being spread farm to farm, and I'm not even mentioning the other environmental concerns that the people of the Towy valley have. Don't you agree with me, Minister, that we cannot have a situation where rural communities in west Wales have to spend hundreds of thousands of pounds to ask a court to help them to merely protect their own farms? Farmers need protection in place. They need support on this, Minister. Green GEN Cymru and contracted surveyors need to adhere to the rules to protect our farms. Will you work with the Cabinet Minister for Enterprise, Connectivity and Energy to ensure this happens, please, and perhaps even visit the Towy valley to meet with the communities there that are so concerned? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you. I won't get drawn on particular court cases, et cetera—you'll understand that I can't comment on those—but you make a very valid point about biosecurity measures, and I will write to the company and others to make sure that they are reminded of their responsibility particularly to respect those.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Llefarydd Llafur Cymru, Vikki Howells.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: The Welsh Labour spokesperson, Vikki Howells.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Cabinet Minister, over lunch today we both attended WWF Cymru's briefing on the implications of extreme weather events such as wildfire and flooding, where we heard from speakers including representatives of the fire service and the farming sector. A key takeaway from that session for me was the vital role that nature-based solutions have to play in protecting communities and farm businesses from the impacts of climate change-related weather events. Given the shared commitments of our parties to increase the use of nature-based solutions across Government action, I'm wondering what steps you might intend to take to mainstream their use in the coming months. Both WWF Cymru and the Fire Brigades Union have come forward with funding proposals to ensure Wales is more resilient and better prepared for extreme weather impacts, and a key element of this proposal is seeking commitment to an extreme weather resilience fund that could look to inject tens of millions of new money into the expansion of preventative spend on nature-based solutions. We're at that time of year when everyone is talking about the budget, so, as those conversations go on, will you commit to making it a priority to expand nature-based solution investment within your portfolio?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Well, not only within my portfolio, as I think there's a huge responsibility across Government on all of us to lean more heavily on nature-based solutions, because we can mix concrete to our heart's content, but, unless we work with the grain of nature, we will always ultimately lose that battle. So, we do have to recalibrate our approach, and we absolutely are committed to those nature-based solutions. The wildfire summit in a few weeks' time will offer, hopefully, the starting gun for some particular work streams around that. I have some particular thoughts around how the sustainable farming scheme and land management can actually support that as well, particularly given the way that farmers stepped up to help fight some of the wildfires that we saw over the summer. Flooding as well, of course—we know there's talk of improving catchment or retaining water through various means in the uplands, et cetera. But key to all of this as well, of course, is it still needs funding, it still needs finance, because the interventions will cost. So, yes, Government has a role to play. Other authorities clearly have a role to play. But nature finance as well, I think, is a key area where we need to be focusing on. I very much intend to build on the work of the previous Government to really focus on that area over the coming months.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Cabinet Minister, I'm really encouraged by your answer there, and I look forward to seeing these developments over the coming months. I think there's particular potential within the optional and collaborative layers of the SFS for that as well.

Turning to another matter, a review of the code of practice for the rearing of game birds for sporting purposes in Wales is overdue, with animal welfare organisations such as the League Against Cruel Sports concerned that this is an issue that is being overlooked. This is perhaps borne out by the data. There were no inspections of game bird farms in either 2023 or 2024 and just four since 2025, and those uncovered two breaches of the code of practice. We also have shocking evidence from Animal Aid site visits of three game bird breeding farms in Wales that found conditions falling far below the standards that we all expect. What assessment has the Welsh Government made of the treatment and welfare conditions of game birds bred and reared to be shot for sport, and what plans do you have to ensure that the code is reviewed to ensure it is fit for purpose?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you for that. I'm not 100 per cent sure where we are on that. I am aware, if I'm correct, and I don't wish to mislead the Senedd, that a review is happening of the evidence at the minute. I'm awaiting advice from officials. Maybe, if you'd allow me, I will write to you to give you an update of where we are, because it is an area that clearly needs to be addressed.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Yes, she's very good. She never does it to me. [Laughter.]

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
You announced at the Royal Welsh Show the national food strategy, which you have got a group working on at the moment, and I commend you for doing that, because it's something that has been missing. But it's really vital that both ends are joined up—the farm gate and the retailer selling to the consumer. Are you confident that you've got the mix right on that group? Because, when I look at the people on there, there doesn't seem to be a major retailer, who, at the end of the day, passes the bulk of the food on to the consumer. And I don't believe you've got a major processor on there either. And those are two key ingredients that are required to build a sustainable chain of supply here in Wales. I hope it'll be successful.

And the other thing that is required is your ability to use legislation to drive improvements in public procurement and nutritional standards. You supported my colleague Peter Fox's Bill when it came to the floor of the Senedd. Will you commit today, as a Minister, that whatever the food strategy group recommends, and if it requires legislation to support those recommendations, you will pilot that through the Senedd as a Government Minister?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you. There were a couple of questions in there. I haven't got the list in front of me of the membership of that group, but we are, you're right, looking at a whole food system, from gate to plate and beyond—well, no, where does it go after that? I'm not sure. [Laughter.] But, certainly, there is a need to make sure that all voices are heard around that table. And I know, of course, that the group itself will be utilising work streams that will draw on experience of others also through other fora and networks. And I know that the chair has engaged widely, to say the least, already, beyond what has been brought together around that particular stakeholder group.

It will have a number of work streams. We want to look at areas around the red meat supply chain in Wales. We want to look at horticulture and growing horticulture, and we want to look at food in schools initially. Those are some of the areas that will be prioritised in the first place. So, clearly, if we're looking at the red meat supply chain, then processors and others will be a big, big part of that conversation.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I didn't hear you refer to the legislation, and I'd be grateful if you'd reply back to me on that, because, as I said, you did support the food Bill when it first came here. Sadly, the Government at the time rejected it. I think it's an important instrument to use to drive up nutritional standards and also local procurement.

But I'd also like to raise with you the point that I raised with you in committee the other day about the fertiliser tax that's coming in in January of this year. That could potentially be devastating to the ability to procure fertiliser to grow the crops for next year's harvest. And at a time when the uncertainty in the middle east is driving up fertiliser prices to double what they should be at this time of year for forward buying, it seems madness to me to actually introduce a fertiliser tax. Will you now lobby the Westminster Government—the point I made to you in committee—to hold that off for at least 12 months, as the National Farmers Union were asking, so that that situation, hopefully, in the middle east can get back to a sense of normality, so that that price pressure can come out of the system and farmers can purchase the fertiliser they need with confidence that there isn't this supertax being applied to it?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Well, after the session we had in committee, I made sure that I did write to the UK Government to make these representations, to make sure that any implications for Welsh agriculture are properly considered and any negative consequences are avoided. My understanding is, of course, that most of the fertiliser coming to the UK is from the EU—so they wouldn't be affected by the carbon border adjustment mechanism—mainly from the Netherlands, Norway, Germany, and Belgium. But there is some coming from beyond, and we need to guard against any negative consequences stemming from that.

To come back to your previous question as well, if we need to legislate on certain areas, we will. I think we need to wait and see what they recommend. I would prefer action that doesn't require legislation in order to get on with it more quickly, but where we do need to legislate, we won't shy away from that.

And on strengthening procurement policy as well, I know that there will be the publication of a new statement on public procurement policy from this Welsh Government soon, and I'm sure the relevant Minister will publish that when it's ready.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Ffynonellau Dŵr Daear
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Groundwater Sources

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 3. Pa gamau mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn eu cymryd i sicrhau bod ffynonellau dŵr daear, y gallai datblygiadau mawr effeithio arnynt, yn cael eu diogelu a'u monitro'n briodol? OQ64604
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 3. What action is the Welsh Government taking to ensure that groundwater sources that could be affected by major developments are appropriately protected and monitored? OQ64604

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Protecting groundwater is essential for safeguarding drinking water supplies, the environment and Wales's long-term water resilience. Planning and environmental permitting processes require risks to groundwater to be assessed and managed. Where risks are identified, Natural Resources Wales can then require mitigation measures, monitoring and ongoing controls to protect water resources.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Diolch. Access to clean and safe groundwater is essential for protecting public health, supporting agriculture and safeguarding our natural environment. As major developments come forward across Wales, it is vital that local communities can feel confident that groundwater sources are being properly monitored and protected. Can you outline how the Welsh Government is working with Natural Resources Wales and the local planning authorities to ensure that groundwater resources are robustly monitored, protected and transparently assessed before major developments are approved?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you for that question. I know that this is a challenge that could occur in a number of different contexts. I hope you'll be reassured that the Welsh Government is working with Natural Resources Wales and local planning authorities through the planning and environmental permitting systems to make sure that groundwater risks are identified and that they are properly assessed and managed before major developments proceed.

We set the national planning policy framework that local planning authorities apply when determining applications, and Natural Resources Wales provide specialist technical advice on groundwater risks as a statutory consultee. Planning authorities can draw on their hydrogeological expertise when they consider whether further investigation or any mitigation or monitoring is needed before a decision is taken. 

Where evidence identifies a specific local risk, local planning authorities and NRW can use their respective planning and permitting functions to make sure that proportionate monitoring and controls are in place during construction and operation. But, ultimately, we will work closely with those bodies to support the consistent and effective application of groundwater protections as a number of different development pressures—and environmental risks, no doubt—evolve.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
This links back to the Member's question, but I want to go a bit more local. The Welsh Water treatment works in Gowerton serves around 58,000 constituents across Gŵyr Abertawe. However, concerns have been raised that proposed housing developments in Gowerton and surrounding areas could place unsustainable pressure on waste water networks and storage capacity.

Natural Resources Wales has already suspended major developments due to rising nitrate levels in the Loughor estuary. Also, local residents, through Save Gowerton from Gridlock, have warned that the proposed 216-home development would exacerbate traffic congestion on Victoria Road. 

What action is the Welsh Government taking to address the concerns identified by NRW and Welsh Water, and to ensure that essential infrastructure in Gowerton is not overwhelmed and that further damage is not caused to our waterways?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you for drawing attention to a very important area here. I won't get drawn on particular local issues, but, more generally, we do know that the nutrient impact on housing delivery is concerning. The Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning and I both recognise the importance of this issue. 

To strengthen leadership and strategic co-ordination to try and address those nutrient-related challenges, the Welsh Government is establishing a new nutrient efficiency and resilience group. That group will bring together key partners and stakeholders, including regulators, water companies, the agricultural sector, environmental organisations and local authority representatives, to provide strategic oversight of nutrient management across Wales.

Its work will focus on both the immediate operational challenges, which are pressing, but also the longer term actions needed to restore and improve the health of our rivers and catchments, helping to deliver a more co-ordinated and whole-system approach to river recovery and environmental improvement, but also, hopefully, unlocking potential developments such as the one that you've referred to.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Ffermydd Teuluol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Family Farms

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 4. Pa gamau y mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn eu cymryd i ddiogelu ffermydd teuluol ym Mrycheiniog Tawe Nedd rhag y pwysau ariannol ac amgylcheddol cynyddol sy'n wynebu amaethyddiaeth? OQ64577
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 4. What action is the Welsh Government taking to protect family farms in Brycheiniog Tawe Nedd from the growing financial and environmental pressures facing agriculture? OQ64577

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: The Welsh Government is supporting family farms in Brycheiniog Tawe Nedd through its £340 million annual budget commitment. To help farmers facing significant pressures this year particularly, we've increased advance payments from 70 per cent to 80 per cent. The sustainable farming scheme is an accessible whole-farm scheme, designed to support the long-term resilience of farms.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you. Resilience means very little if our family farms cannot survive. Farmers across Brycheiniog Tawe Nedd have endured an incredibly difficult year, as I'm sure you're fully aware, through droughts, wildfires, rising costs and the continued threat of bovine TB, whilst also being expected to adapt to the new sustainable farming scheme. These aren't simply businesses; they produce our food, manage our countryside, support thousands of jobs and keep our rural communities alive. Yet too often farmers tell me they feel these policies have been done to them, rather than being developed with them. Will you guarantee that food production and the survival of the Welsh family farm will be at the heart of your decisions? And also, will you ensure that environmental ambitions work alongside productive farming rather than adding further costs and regulation to the very people we depend upon to feed us and look after our countryside?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Yes I will, because family farms, as you say, are the backbone of our rural communities in Brycheiniog Tawe Nedd and the rest of Wales as well, and we recognise the significant pressures that those businesses are facing. That's why we have been flexible, for example around the control of agricultural pollution regulations, in allowing a longer period to clear some of the slurry stores that farms have, but to do so in a responsible way, in a managed way, in a controlled way. Natural Resources Wales support that approach, because they recognise that there would be additional environmental risks from those stores overspilling or failing, which would be even more catastrophic. So, I'd like to think that we are being pragmatic and practical where we can be.

I spent the summer visiting a number of agricultural shows, and there were three things, basically, that farmers were asking for. One is certainty in a hugely uncertain world, and we are trying to deliver that with our commitment to long-term funding for farming. But they also ask for flexibility. When circumstances change, such as the drought we saw over the summer, then maybe we need to look at the way we ask farms to do things. We've introduced derogations within the SFS in terms of some of the things that they have to achieve directly as a consequence of some of those extreme weather events. The third element was general support. If you look at the red tape review, one of the steps that we've taken, then hopefully we're demonstrating that as well. So yes, we do need to make sure that farming is resilient and is sustainable for the future, and I will do everything I can to achieve that.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I know that many Members were at the NFU reception last week, and hearing the union and farmers thank the Minister for a number of decisions this Welsh Government has taken so far to support them speaks volumes. For the first time, farmers feel heard. Plaid Cymru's manifesto commits to rural-proofing our communities, including those in my constituency of Brycheiniog Tawe Nedd. Could we have some information on the progress of the rural development strategy for Wales and how this will tackle poverty and create new economic and social opportunities for my constituents?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you very much for the question. I think it's very appropriate that the enterprise Minister is sat next to me, because I fully hope that this will be a joint endeavour. But we are looking to increase that particular focus on some of the communities that feel maybe that they have been marginalised in some of these discussions in the past. But certainly, we want to consider that statutory duty to make sure that, when it comes to creating policy or making funding decisions, for example, that balance and that consideration in the round is taken. It isn't about setting one part of Wales against another. It's making sure that every part of Wales has a fair hearing, and that's certainly, when it comes to the rural-proofing duty, something that we want to achieve. You will be aware that we are consulting at the minute, that there is an opportunity for people to feed in around those proposals, and I very much look forward to receiving those.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Wydnwch Gwledig a Chynaliadwyedd
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Rural Resilience and Sustainability
